# 1 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_008_page_001.jpg

---

1. And Judas heard of the fame of the Romans, that they were very strong and that they accepted all who came to them, and that they made a league of friendship with all who put themselves in their hands,
2. and that they were very strong. And men told him of their wars and their brave deeds which they did in Galatia, how they conquered them and brought them under tribute;
3. and what things they did in the land of Spain, to bring into their possession the mines of silver and of gold that were there;
4. and how they had gotten possession of all the place by their counsel and their patience, even though the place was very far from them; and kings who came from the end of the earth against them they crushed and struck, and the rest paid tribute to them every year;
5. and Philip and Perseus king of the Macedonians, and the rest who lifted up themselves against them, were vanquished and brought under their power;
6. and Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, who came against them for battle with a hundred and twenty elephants and with horsemen and with chariots and with a very great army — he was defeated by them;
7. and they took him alive and appointed that he and such kings as reigned after him should pay a great tribute and give hostages and a parcel of land —
8. even the land of India and Media and Lydia and some of the fairest lands of his, which they took and gave to King Eumenes.
9. And the men of Greece had taken counsel to come and destroy them;
10. but the matter was made known to them, and they sent against them one of their captains, and he fought against them and many of them fell; and they led away their wives and their children captive, and plundered them, and took possession of their land, and tore down their strongholds, and made them slaves to this day.
11. And the other kingdoms and islands, as many as ever rose against them, they destroyed and made slaves;
12. but with their friends and those who relied on them they kept friendship; and they became rulers of kingdoms both near and far, and all who heard their name were afraid of them.
13. Those whom they wish to help and to make kings they make kings; and those whom they wish to remove they remove; and they were greatly exalted.
14. And with all this not one of them put on a crown, nor did they clothe themselves with purple, to make themselves great.
15. And they had made for themselves a senate house, and every day three hundred and twenty men sat in council, deliberating always for the people, to govern them well.
16. And they entrust their government to one man every year, to rule over all their land, and all obey that one man, and there is no envy or jealousy among them.
17. And Judas chose Eupolemus son of John, son of Accos, and Jason son of Eleazar, and he sent them to Rome to establish friendship and alliance with them,
18. and to lift the yoke from them; for they saw that the kingdom of the Greeks was keeping Israel in complete slavery.
19. And they traveled to Rome — a very long journey — and they entered the senate house, and answered and said:
20. "Judas, called Maccabeus, and his brothers and the people of the Jews have sent us to you to make with you an alliance and peace, and to register us as your allies and friends."
21. And the matter was pleasing before them.
22. And this is the copy of the letter which they wrote on bronze tablets and sent to Jerusalem, that there it might be for them a memorial of peace and of alliance:
23. "May it be well with the Romans and with the nation of the Jews at sea and on land, forever; and sword and enemy be far from them.
24. And if there comes war first against Rome, or any of her allies in all her dominion,
25. the nation of the Jews shall fight along with them heartily, as the occasion shall prescribe for them.
26. And to those who make war they shall not give nor supply grain, weapons, silver, or ships; and Rome decided so; and they shall observe the stipulations without receiving any reward.
27. In the same way, if war come first against the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall fight along with them heartily, as the occasion shall prescribe for them;
28. and to those who make war against them there shall not be given grain, weapons, silver, or ships; and Rome decided so; and they shall observe these stipulations without guile.
29. On these terms the Romans make the covenant with the people of the Jews.
30. But if hereafter the one party or the other shall see fit to add or take away anything, they shall do it at their pleasure, and whatever they shall add or take away shall be binding.
31. And as touching the wrongs which King Demetrius does to them, we have written to him saying, 'Wherefore have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends and allies the Jews?
32. If therefore they plead any more against you, we will do judgment for them and will fight against you by sea and by land.'"
